title: Did you know… the early Church didn’t start with power?
paragraphs: Did you know… the early Church didn’t start with power?
It started with unity.

Not miracles first.
Not influence.
Not numbers.
Unity.
“They were all together in one place…” (Acts 2:1)
That’s where heaven touched earth.

Before the fire fell…
Before 3,000 were saved…
Before the bold preaching…
There was a room full of people who chose each other over ego.

No platforms.
No titles.
No competition.
Just hearts aligned under one Name—Jesus.
But here’s what we miss…
We chase power without protecting unity.

We want the anointing…
But we resist forgiveness.
We want revival…
But we harbor offense.
We want God to move…
But we won’t reconcile.
And heaven waits.
Because the Spirit doesn’t rest on division.
Psalm 133 says unity is where God commands the blessing.

Not suggests.
Commands.
And that blessing? It’s life. It’s presence. It’s power.

So when the disciples humbled themselves…
Prayed together…
Stayed together…
That’s when the fire came.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because unity is not something we manufacture.
It’s something Jesus died to create.

On the cross, He didn’t just forgive you—
He tore down the walls between us.

Sin divides.
Christ restores.

And the same Spirit that fell in Acts 2?
He still moves today—
But He’s looking for hearts that are surrendered, not superior.
So let me ask you…

Who do you need to forgive?
What pride do you need to lay down?
Where has division replaced devotion?
Come back.

Not just to power—
But to the posture that invites it.

Unity.
Humility.
Jesus at the center.
Because revival doesn’t begin on a stage.
It begins in a surrendered heart.
